Section 3 • Transmitted Flux

3.7 Summary

For quick reference, we collect here the main equations of the transmitted-flux calculation, ordered from the final observable quantities down to the local gas properties from which they are constructed. The full construction is: \begin{align*} \lambda'(\vec{x},\Lambda) \,\rightarrow\, \nu_j(\vec{x},\Lambda) \,\rightarrow\, \phi_{ij}(\vec{x},\Lambda) \,\rightarrow\, \tau_{ij}(\vec{x}_{\perp}, \Lambda) \,\rightarrow\, T_{ij}(\vec{x}_{\perp}, \Lambda) \,\rightarrow\, \delta_{j}(\vec{x}_{\perp}, \Lambda) \end{align*}

For a given realization \(s\) and line \(j\) – with the contextual species index \(i\) suppressed – the overflux is: \begin{align} \delta_{j}^{(s)}\!\left(\vec{x}_{\perp},\Lambda\right) + 1 &\;=\; \frac{ F_{j}^{(s)}\!\left(\vec{x}_{\perp},\Lambda\right) }{ F_{0}^{(s)}\!\left(\vec{x}_{\perp},\Lambda\right)\bar{T}_{j}\!(\Lambda) } = \frac{ T_{j}^{(s)}\!\left(\vec{x}_{\perp},\Lambda\right) }{ \bar{T}_{j}\!(\Lambda) }, \quad \mathrm{with}\quad \bar{T}_{j}\!(\Lambda) \coloneqq \left\langle T_{j}^{(s)}\left(\vec{x}_{\perp},\Lambda\right) \right\rangle_{\mathrm{ens}}. \tag{3.37} \end{align}

If several lines contribute simultaneously, the total overflux can be written in terms of the line-by-line overfluxes as: \begin{align} &\delta^{(s)}(\vec{x}_\perp, \Lambda) =\frac{1}{1 + \mathcal{C}(\Lambda)}\sum_{p=0}^{L} \mathcal{S}_p^{(s)}(\vec{x}_{\perp},\,\Lambda) \tag{3.38} \end{align}

Where we have defined: \begin{align} &\mathcal{S}_0^{(s)}(\Lambda) \coloneqq -\mathcal{C}(\Lambda), \qquad \mathcal{S}_p^{(s)}(\vec{x}_{\perp},\,\Lambda) \coloneqq \sum_{1\le j_1<\cdots<j_p\le L}\; \prod_{r=1}^{p} \delta_{j_r}^{(s)}\!\left(\vec{x}_\perp,\Lambda\right) \quad \textrm{(order $p$)}, \qquad 1\le p\le L, \notag \end{align}

and \begin{align} \mathcal{C}(\Lambda) &\coloneqq \sum_{1\le j_1<j_2\le L} C_{j_1 j_2}(\Lambda) + \sum_{1\le j_1<j_2<j_3\le L} C_{j_1 j_2 j_3}(\Lambda) + \cdots + C_{1 2 \cdots L}(\Lambda), \tag{3.39} \\ &\quad\mathrm{where}\quad C_{j_1 \cdots j_n}(\Lambda) \coloneqq \left\langle \delta_{j_1}^{(s)}\cdots\delta_{j_n}^{(s)} \right\rangle_{\mathrm{ens}}. \notag \end{align}

The transmission is obtained from the optical depth, and the transmitted flux by attenuating the emitted continuum \(F_0(\Lambda)\) by the transmission factor: \begin{align} F_{ij}\!\left(\vec{x}_{\perp},\Lambda\right) &= F_0(\Lambda)\,T_{ij}\!\left(\vec{x}_{\perp},\Lambda\right) , \quad T_{ij}\!\left(\vec{x}_{\perp},\Lambda\right) = \exp\!\left[-\tau_{ij}\!\left(\vec{x}_{\perp},\Lambda\right)\right]. \tag{3.40} \end{align}

In the straight-line approximation, the optical depth along the line of sight can be computed as: \begin{align} \tau_{ij}\!\left(\vec{x}_{\perp},\Lambda\right) = \mathcal{C}_j \int_{x_{\parallel,\mathrm{em}}}^{x_{\parallel,\mathrm{f}}} \frac{ n_{i\,\mathrm{com}}\!\left(\vec{x}_{\perp},x'_{\parallel}\right) }{ a\!\left(\vec{x}_{\perp},x'_{\parallel}\right)^{3} } \; \phi_{ij}\!\left(\vec{x}_{\perp},x'_{\parallel},\Lambda\right) \; a\!\left(\vec{x}_{\perp},x'_{\parallel}\right)\, dx'_{\parallel}, \qquad \mathcal{C}_j \equiv \frac{e^{2}f_j}{4\varepsilon_{0}m_e c}. \tag{3.41} \end{align}

The local absorption line profile kernel is described by the Voigt profile: \begin{align} \phi_{ij}\!\left(\vec{x},\Lambda\right) = V\!\left( \nu_j\!\left(\vec{x},\Lambda\right); \sigma_{ij}\!\left(\vec{x}\right), \gamma_j\!\left(\vec{x}\right) \right), \tag{3.42} \end{align} where the frequency offset is \begin{align} \nu_j\!\left(\vec{x},\Lambda\right) = c\left( \frac{1}{\lambda'\!\left(\vec{x},\Lambda\right)} - \frac{1}{\lambda_j} \right). \tag{3.43} \end{align}

The Doppler factor is defined as: \begin{align} \Dop(\vec{x}) \coloneqq \sqrt{\frac{1-\beta(\vec{x})}{1+\beta(\vec{x})}}, \qquad \beta(\vec{x}) \coloneqq \frac{v_{i\,\parallel}(\vec{x})}{c}. \qquad \textrm{If } \quad v_{i\,\parallel} \ll c \quad \longrightarrow \quad \Dop^{-1}(\vec{x}) \approx 1+ \beta(\vec{x}) \tag{3.44} \end{align}

  • If \(\Lambda=\lambda_{\mathrm{obs}}\), then \begin{align} \lambda'\!\left(\vec{x},\Lambda\right) = \lambda_{\mathrm{obs}}\, \frac{a(\vec{x})}{a_{\mathrm{obs}}}\, \Dop^{-1}(\vec{x}). \qquad \lambda_\mathrm{obs} \in \left[ \lambda_{j,\mathrm{min}} \; , \; \lambda_{j,\mathrm{max}} \frac{a_f}{a_{\mathrm{em}}} \right]. \tag{3.45} \end{align}

  • If \(\Lambda=v_{\dagger}\), then \begin{align} \lambda'_j\!\left(\vec{x},\Lambda\right) = \lambda_j\, \exp\!\left(\frac{v_{\dagger}}{c}\right)\, \frac{a(\vec{x})}{a_f}\, \Dop^{-1}(\vec{x}). \qquad v_\dagger \in \left[ 0 \; , \; c\ln\left(\frac{a_f}{a_{\mathrm{em}}}\right) \right]. \tag{3.46} \end{align}

  • If \(\Lambda=x\), then \begin{align} \lambda'\left(\vec{x},\Lambda\right) &\approx \lambda_j\left[ 1+ \frac{1}{c} \left( \frac{H(z_{\mathrm{box}})}{1+z_{\mathrm{box}}}(\vec{x}-x_\dagger) + v_{i\,\parallel}(\vec{x}) \right) \right]. \tag{3.47} \end{align}

The Gaussian and Lorentzian widths entering the Voigt profile are \begin{align} \sigma_{ij}(\vec{x}) &= \frac{b_i(\vec{x})}{\sqrt{2}\lambda_j}, \qquad b_i(\vec{x}) = \sqrt{ b_{i\,\mathrm{th}}^{2}(\vec{x}) + b_{i\,\mathrm{turb}}^{2}(\vec{x}) }, \qquad b_{i\,\mathrm{th}}(\vec{x}) = \sqrt{\frac{2k_B T_i(\vec{x})}{m_i}}, \tag{3.48} \\[0.3em] \gamma_j(\vec{x}) &= \frac{A_j + A_{j\,\mathrm{coll}}(\vec{x})}{4\pi}. \tag{3.49} \end{align}
